lines.say: Organic reactions turn one functional group into another.
Here is ethene. The double bond is like a pair of arms.

draw.alt: Ethene with a C=C double bond

lines.say: Add water. One bond opens, and each carbon grabs a new group.

draw.alt: The double bond opens and H and OH add on

lines.say: Nothing is lost, so addition has 100 percent atom economy.
Hydration needs a phosphoric acid catalyst, steam, about 300 degrees and high pressure.
Hydrogenation needs a nickel catalyst. Bromine water going colourless tests for C double bond C.
In substitution, one atom or group is swapped for another.
Heat bromoethane with sodium hydroxide. The bromine is swapped for O H.

draw.alt: Br leaves and OH takes its place

lines.say: With ammonia instead, the halogen is swapped for N H two, making an amine.
Alkanes swap an H for a halogen, but only in U V light.
Oxidising an alcohol removes the H on the O H and an H on that carbon.
lines.write: needs H on the C–OH carbon

lines.say: Acidified dichromate goes from orange to green when it works.

draw.alt: Dichromate changes from orange to green

lines.say: Primary goes all the way. First an aldehyde, then a carboxylic acid.
Secondary stops at a ketone.
Tertiary just sits there. No H on that carbon, so it stays orange.

draw.alt: Three test tubes: primary and secondary turn green, tertiary stays orange

lines.say: In condensation, two molecules join and a small molecule, usually water, leaves.
Ethanoic acid and ethanol join. The O H from the acid and the H from the alcohol leave.

draw.alt: Acid and alcohol join to form an ester, water leaves

lines.say: Heat under reflux with concentrated sulfuric acid as the catalyst.
An acid and an amine join the same way, making an amide link.
Hydrolysis is the reverse. Water splits the ester back into acid and alcohol.
Atom economy asks how much reactant mass ends up in the product you want.
Route A, hydration. 46 over 28 plus 18. That is 100 percent.
Route B, substitution. 46 over 64.5 plus 40. Only 44 percent.

draw.alt: Bars comparing 100 percent and 44 percent atom economy

lines.say: More than half of route B's reactant mass becomes sodium chloride waste.
Percentage yield compares what you got with the most you could get.
12.0 grams of ethanoic acid is 0.200 moles. It is the limiting reactant.
One to one ratio, so at most 0.200 moles of ester, which is 17.6 grams.
She collected 14.1 grams. 14.1 over 17.6 is 80.1 percent.

draw.alt: Bar showing 80.1 percent of the theoretical yield collected

lines.say: Atom economy is on paper. Yield is what happened in the lab.
Tertiary alcohols do not oxidise to ketones. They do not react at all.
No water on the right of an esterification? Then it isn't balanced.
Use the limiting reactant for theoretical yield, never the excess one.
Dichromate goes dark green. Permanganate goes pale.
Addition opens a C double bond C and keeps everything.
Substitution swaps. Condensation joins and loses water. Hydrolysis splits with water.
Primary goes all the way, secondary stops at a ketone, tertiary sits there.
Learn the conditions in pairs, like nickel for hydrogenation and U V for alkanes.
